pdm-pericarditis-electrolytes-drugs: Which space does pericarditis inflame?
Between the visceral and parietal pericardium
Which PR change appears in most leads in pericarditis?
PR-segment depression
Which PR change appears in aVR in pericarditis?
PR-segment elevation
What ST pattern does pericarditis produce?
Global concave ST elevation
Where may ST depression still appear in pericarditis?
Only in aVR and V1
Which findings rule out pericarditis?
ST depression outside aVR and V1, or any Q wave
What is benign early repolarization also called?
Normal variant ST elevation
In whom is benign early repolarization mostly seen?
Young men
What clinical significance does early repolarization carry?
None
What is terminal QRS notching in early repolarization called?
A J wave, or fishhook sign
Which lead separates pericarditis from early repolarization?
Lead V6
Which V6 ST-to-T ratio suggests pericarditis?
Greater than 25%
Which V6 ST-to-T ratio suggests early repolarization?
Less than 25%
Which channels does Brugada syndrome affect?
Sodium channels of the right ventricular outflow tract
In whom is Brugada syndrome most common?
Young men of Southeast Asian descent
What shape is type 1 Brugada?
Coved (convex) ST elevation
What shape is type 2 Brugada?
Saddleback ST elevation
Which leads show Brugada findings?
V1 to V3 only
Why is an infarction hard to see in a left bundle branch block?
Wide QRS with global ST and T changes
Which criteria find an infarction in a bundle branch block or paced rhythm?
Sgarbossa's criteria
How much concordant ST elevation meets Sgarbossa's criteria?
1 mm or more
Which concordant change in V1 to V3 meets Sgarbossa's criteria?
ST depression of 1 mm or more
How much discordant ST elevation meets Sgarbossa's criteria?
5 mm or more
What precedes each wide QRS in a ventricular paced rhythm?
A pacing spike
Which way do T waves point in a paced rhythm?
Opposite the QRS (contralateral)
What occurs first as the body cools toward 35 degrees Celsius?
Sinus bradycardia
Below which temperature do Osborn waves appear?
32 degrees Celsius (90 degrees Fahrenheit)
What are Osborn waves often mistaken for?
An ST-elevation infarction
What is preexcitation?
Early ventricular activation through an accessory pathway
What is the accessory pathway in Wolff-Parkinson-White called?
The bundle of Kent
What is the Wolff-Parkinson-White triad?
Short PR, wide QRS and a delta wave
What is a delta wave?
A slurred upstroke of the QRS
Why is the PR interval short in preexcitation?
The impulse bypasses the atrioventricular node
Which Wolff-Parkinson-White type has a positive QRS in V1?
Type A, a left-sided Kent bundle
Which Wolff-Parkinson-White type has a negative QRS in V1?
Type B, a right-sided Kent bundle
What does orthodromic reentry produce?
A regular narrow-complex tachycardia
What does antidromic reentry produce?
A regular, monomorphic, wide tachycardia
How does the antidromic circuit run?
Down the accessory pathway, up the normal pathway
What is the early sign of hyperkalemia?
Peaked, symmetric T waves
What is the end-stage hyperkalemia pattern?
A sine wave
Below which potassium is hypokalemia defined?
3.5 mEq/L
Which wave becomes prominent in hypokalemia?
The U wave
Which phase does hypocalcemia prolong?
Phase 2
What happens to the T wave in hypocalcemia?
It stays normal in shape and duration
What happens to the QTc in hypercalcemia?
It shortens
What happens to the ST segment in hypercalcemia?
It shortens, pushing the T wave against the QRS
Do sodium changes alter the tracing?
No
What is the commonest finding in hyperthyroidism?
Sinus tachycardia
What is the second commonest finding in hyperthyroidism?
Atrial fibrillation
What voltage change does hypothyroidism cause?
Global low-voltage QRS complexes
What does digoxin toxicity inhibit?
The sodium-potassium pump
What is the most common abnormality in digoxin toxicity?
Frequent premature ventricular complexes
Which actions does amiodarone combine?
Sodium, potassium and calcium channel block plus beta blockade
Which phase does amiodarone slow, prolonging the QT?
Phase 3
What causes tachycardia in a tricyclic overdose?
Anticholinergic activity
Which pattern is associated with pulmonary embolism?
S1Q3T3
Why is the rate fast in pulmonary embolism?
Hypoxia activates the sympathetic nervous system
Which axis shift does pulmonary embolism cause?
A rightward shift
Which two tracing changes does a tricyclic overdose produce?
QT prolongation and tachycardia
